name: Canthaxanthin
short: Case report: fatal aplastic anaemia after oral canthaxanthin for tanning. Retinal crystals: 8 of 32 light-dermatosis/vitiligo patients on it and beta-carotene orally. Other study: some lasted 7 years.
text: A case report described aplastic anaemia with a fatal outcome in a previously healthy young woman after she took canthaxanthin by mouth for skin tanning; the authors noted that the safety of oral doses had not been investigated in humans and that the frequency of adverse effects such as bone marrow suppression is unknown. A case series describes canthaxanthin retinopathy as its most frequent adverse effect, while calling it rare. In a study of 32 patients with light-related skin disease or vitiligo treated with oral canthaxanthin and beta-carotene, 8 had crystalline deposits in the inner retina around the macula, linked to the total canthaxanthin dose but not to treatment duration, with no deterioration of visual function. In a follow-up study of 9 patients, the deposits decreased significantly only after about 26 months, some remained seven years after canthaxanthin was stopped, and the authors concluded that the retinopathy is reversible; however, a later case report described a woman who took canthaxanthin for tanning for 7 years whose crystals persisted, though fewer, 4 years after she presented, with retinal pigment epithelial detachments that the authors interpreted as persistent damage. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
